A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SG-ULA research work. All 23 pages of v2 and 24 pages of v3, including Appendices A–F and both tables, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports mathematical examples, convergence theorems, proofs, and analytical complexity comparisons. Neither the main text nor the appendices report original empirical outcomes.

after.justification: v3 remains theoretical. Its added Gaussian-mixture example is analytical; references to evaluating samplers concern cited work, not original experiments.

M1.justification: The SG-ULA update in Equation (7), subgradient selection, Gaussian noise, and Euler–Maruyama construction are unchanged. The revised guarantees and additional assumptions do not introduce a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts training or empirical evaluation on datasets or test scenarios. The new Gaussian-mixture/L1-prior example in Section 4.1 illustrates theoretical applicability.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparison works: Lehec, Johnston et al., Habring et al., and Fruehwirth et al. The additional A5 row describes the proposed method under different assumptions, not another comparator.

E3.justification: No experimental protocols are introduced or revised. The new inverse-temperature restriction and revised stepsize/iteration bounds are theoretical conditions, not evaluation settings.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, sensitivity experiments, robustness tests, or empirical case studies. The added potential examples and contraction analysis are mathematical developments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Changes to moment bounds concern theoretical estimates rather than statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The analytical result entries change substantially. Table 1 replaces the general W1/W2 complexities ε^(-2)/ε^(-4) with ε^(-4)/ε^(-8) under A2, and adds an A5 row reporting ε^(-2)/ε^(-4). Comparator entries remain unchanged. These are theoretical complexity results, not measured performance changes; the A5 W1 entry is not established by the stated theorems.

T1.justification: v3 removes v2's separate W1 discretization lemma and reuses the retained W2 estimate, weakening Theorems 1–2 from λ^(1/2)/λ^(1/4) to λ^(1/4)/λ^(1/8). It adds Assumption A5, the temperature restriction (18), and a conditional λ^(1/4) W2 theorem with supporting contraction proofs. It also revises Brownian-noise and dimension terms, contraction constants, and Table 2, and adds the Gaussian-mixture example. The excess-risk theorem is retained as Theorem 4.

C1.justification: The central convergence guarantees are materially narrowed: the general rates weaken, while the former W2 rate receives a separate guarantee under stronger conditions. The abstract additionally emphasizes replacing Lipschitz/Hölder regularity with geometric one-sided Lipschitz control. Section 7 nevertheless retains the old, unqualified rate claims.

C2.justification: Sections 2.2 and 6.2.2 add an interpretation of why geometric assumptions can avoid deterioration associated with low Hölder regularity. Section 5.1 explains the temperature limitation of the stronger result and recommends the general W2 theorem when optimization requires freely choosing large β.

D1.justification: No implementation, hardware, runtime, code-access, or data-access information is added or revised. Changes to symbolic constants and admissible parameters belong to the theoretical analysis.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting the mixture example and high-diffusivity contraction, introduces Section 6.6 on Euler approximations and lower bounds, and sharpens its contrast with Hölder-dependent guarantees. The existing sampling-literature review and comparison works remain.

P1.justification: The abstract and selected explanations are expanded, new example and literature subsections are inserted, and the proof roadmap and numbering are adjusted. Most prose and the overall section/appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 splits the proposed-work entry into A2 and A5 rows. Table 2 changes formula spacing and row layout to accommodate revised expressions. Both versions retain the same single-column presentation and contain no figures.

improvement.justification: v3 removes v2's defective W1 argument, which omits an initial constant, restores missing noise/dimension terms, and gives more conservative general rates. However, Section 7 retains the old rates, Table 1 reports an unsupported A5 W1 complexity, and the new Equation (12) incorrectly uses αx/|x|₁ for the multidimensional L1-penalty gradient. These substantive repairs coexist with unresolved and newly introduced correctness issues, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
